title: SurroundOcc: Multi-Camera 3D Occupancy Prediction for Autonomous Driving
grouping: Four columns with bold two-line headings across the top (multi-camera features, multi-scale feature aggregation, 3D volume features, occupancy prediction); three scale rows run left to right, with a fourth row added in the volume and prediction columns. A detail panel of the 2D-to-3D block hangs below it inside a thin black frame whose trapezoid lines join the block, and a dashed grey legend box explains the two arrow colours.
shapes_depth: Multi-scale camera features are three stacked levels of thick flat slabs in saturated pastel colours (green, grey, blue, red, purple, yellow) rising from a 2x3 mosaic of camera photos via an orange up-arrow. '2D to 3D' blocks are pale-yellow rounded boxes with 'x6', 'x3', 'x1'. 3D volume features are salmon cube stacks that grow scale by scale (1, 2x2, 4x4, 4x4x deeper) with blue down-arrows between them and shape labels HxWxZ, 2Hx2Wx2Z, 4Hx4Wx4Z, 8Hx8Wx8Z on their output arrows. Each scale ends in a 3-D voxel render of the occupied scene, larger at finer scales. The detail panel is a flat stack of tinted rounded bars (cross-view attention, add & norm, feed forward, 3D convolution) with residual arrows on the right.
proposed_highlight: The predicted occupancy is the visual payload: voxel renders in semantic colours fill the whole right column and grow with resolution; the proposed lifting block is expanded once in the inset rather than coloured differently.
lesson: Show the coarse-to-fine decoder as a column of cube volumes that grow scale by scale with HxWxZ size labels, each feeding a voxel render of the occupancy at that scale, so the multi-scale outputs read as a stack of increasingly detailed 3-D scenes.
notes: Venue ICCV 2023 from the arXiv comment 'Accepted to ICCV 2023' (venue_source: arxiv-journal-ref). The whole figure is a single raster image in the PDF (refs crop recorded one embedded image covering the crop), so kb measure cannot separate photos from drawing: photo_share is null and the palette includes the embedded photos and renders.

measured.source: computed: paperfig kb measure (non-white pixels of a <= 800 px thumbnail, white = min(R,G,B) >= 245, minus the embedded images recorded by `refs crop` (images_px; their share is photo_share, null without a record); chromatic (RGB spread > 20) and neutral pixels clustered separately by PIL median-cut + k-means (k=8 / 3); clusters within dE00 4 merged; kept if >= 0.02 of chromatic pixels / neutral ones if >= 0.03 of all non-white pixels; share = fraction of the non-photo non-white pixels)
